plain.text: In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers, including Barnabas and Saul. While they were worshipping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." After fasting and praying, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.

Sent by the Holy Spirit, they sailed to Cyprus and preached in the synagogues, with John Mark helping them. At Paphos they met a sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus (Elymas), an attendant of the governor, Sergius Paulus, who wanted to hear God's word. Elymas tried to turn the governor from the faith. Saul, also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, said he was an enemy of everything right and would be blind for a time. Immediately darkness came over him. When the governor saw what happened, he believed, amazed at the teaching about the Lord.

Paul and his companions sailed on; John Mark left them and returned to Jerusalem. In Pisidian Antioch they went to the synagogue on the Sabbath. Paul was invited to speak. He told the story of God choosing Israel, rescuing them from Egypt, giving them judges and kings, and especially King David, from whose descendants God brought Israel the Saviour, Jesus, as he promised. John the Baptist prepared the way. The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognise Jesus and asked Pilate to have him executed, fulfilling the prophets. But God raised him from the dead, and he was seen by many. "Through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you. Through him everyone who believes is set free from every sin, which the law of Moses could not do." He warned them not to scoff at what God was doing.

People invited them to speak again the next Sabbath. Many followed Paul and Barnabas, who urged them to continue in God's grace. The next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered. Some leaders were filled with jealousy and spoke abusively against Paul. Paul and Barnabas answered boldly: "We had to speak the word of God to you first. Since you reject it, we now turn to the Gentiles. For the Lord said, 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'" The Gentiles were glad and honoured the word, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed. The word spread through the region. But opponents stirred up persecution and drove them out. They shook the dust off their feet and went to Iconium. And the disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.

summary.bigIdea: The Holy Spirit sends Paul and Barnabas on their first journey, and the good news reaches both Jews and Gentiles.
points: The church in Antioch fasts, prays and sends out Barnabas and Saul (Paul).
Paul tells Israel's story leading to Jesus, through whom sins are forgiven.
Many Gentiles rejoice and believe, though persecution follows.
summary.reflection: The church sent Paul and Barnabas after worshipping and praying. How could prayer shape your big decisions?
